html:
The Hupa are an Athabaskan-speaking people of the lower Trinity River in north-west California, in the valley they call Natinook. They lived in villages of cedar plank houses, depending on salmon and acorns. Wealth was counted in white deerskins, large obsidian blades and dentalium shells, displayed at the White Deerskin and Jump dances that renew the world each year. Their neighbours were the Yurok and Karuk, whose languages are unrelated but whose way of life was much the same, and to the north the Tolowa, who speak a related language.

Gold miners poured into the Trinity country in 1850, during the Gold Rush. Unlike most California peoples, the Hupa kept their valley, which became the Hoopa Valley Reservation in 1864. See also Athabaskan.
